Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 537 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2018) 
 
 
Introduction 
Wildlife Management Unity 537 is an area of boreal forest, agricultural land, and river valleys in northwest Alberta. 
This unit contains resident populations of moose, white-tailed deer, mule deer, elk, and intermittent transient 
caribou. The WMU is important for Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal hunting interests, and encapsulates Paddle 
Prairie Metis Settlement. 
 
Survey Method 
Alberta Environment and Parks conducted an aerial ungulate survey in February 2018 to provide an updated 
estimate on ungulate populations within the unit. The primary objective of the survey was to provide an updated 
moose population estimate. The survey was conducted using Distance Sampling methodology utilizing two Bell 
206 Jet Rangers from February 16 – 18th. Moose were classified by sex and age class (calf or adult), and other 
wildlife sightings were recorded. 
 
Results 
Survey crews flew 149 transects for a total of 1363 kilometres of surveyed transect. A total of 178 moose were 
observed on transect (85 cows, 45 calves, 40 bulls, and 8 unclassified) for a bull:cow:calf ratio of 47:100:53. The 
population estimate and density information is found in Table 1. Survey crews also observed 47 white-tailed deer, 
62 elk (although many were observed off transect), and 0 mule deer. More detailed demographic information is not 
available for these populations due to low sample sizes.

Discussion 
The moose population in WMU 537 appears to have declined slightly from the most recent population estimate, 
and is slightly lowered than expected. However, the population does not appear to be drastically reduced, and is in 
line with the first estimate of this unit. Bull availability remains within management objectives, and calf productivity 
is quite high which indicates opportunity for population growth if overwinter calf survival is high.
